correctness.rationale: Reconstructed if-and-only-if P3 convexity criterion: each omitted subdivision vertex cannot have both original endpoints selected (forcing every internal edge of U), and each omitted original vertex can meet at most one selected edge-vertex. Hence edges internal to W=V\U form a matching, matched vertices disallow any cross choice, unmatched vertices independently take one of d_U(w) cross edges or none. This proves the exact weighted sum for every host. For K_n, matching counts are factorial ratios, cross choices (1+u z)^{w-2j}, giving A_n(z). Exponential labelled matching product and sum over u give exp(t+t^2/2+t e^t); counting external degree<=1 bounds |C|<=n+C(u,2), equality only u=n-1 with one external cross-edge. Independently enumerated every subset of S(K_n) for n=2,3,4,5 and checked the full polynomial and n(n-1) extremizers; counts 7,29,143,797. These checks are bounded; the bijection and formal EGF prove generality.
residual_risks: Only one subdivision per host edge and P3 convexity; geodetic/cycle convexities not covered.
No general efficient exact counting algorithm for arbitrary hosts.

value.rationale: The P3 convex-set count is algorithmically challenging in general; the submitted exact all-host decomposition and explicit complete-host EGF provide structurally useful enumeration for a natural incidence-graph family, while the top-coefficient gap and n(n-1) rigidity are independent extremal information. This is not a tiny arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: No claim for arbitrary convexities, iterative subdivisions or faster generic counting.

final_claim: For every finite simple host H, P3-convex sets of its once-subdivided graph are enumerated by a chosen original-vertex subset U, mandatory internal edges and a matching on H[V\U] with independent cross-edge choices. For K_n, exact size polynomial A_n(z) and EGF of totals exp(t+t^2/2+t e^t); for n>=3, max proper size is N-(n-1) with exactly n(n-1) extremizers.
limitations: Simple undirected host graphs and once-subdivision only; exact generating function for complete hosts only.
